text: The allied health framework describes shared clinical governance responsibility and accountability for quality, continuous improvement and risk minimisation, with flexibility for local implementation across diverse services.

The active NSW policy directive requires NSW Health services to implement systems and processes supporting clinical governance programs, with defined accountabilities and a safety-system approach aligned with national safety and quality requirements.

The 2024 Victorian framework provides best-practice guidance on clinical governance roles, systems, reporting, safety culture, consumer-centred decision-making and accountability across an expanded range of healthcare sectors.
SA Health publishes a system clinical governance framework intended to support governance of safe and high-quality care across its health system.

WA describes clinical governance as integrated with corporate governance and identifies partnering with consumers, a safe environment, governance leadership and culture, safety and quality improvement systems, and clinical performance and effectiveness as core components.

The THS service-planning and performance framework establishes system responsibilities, accountability and performance expectations and provides a public governance source, but it is not a direct substitute for the underlying clinical governance framework.

ACT clinical system governance arrangements operate at whole-of-system level and include system safety, quality, monitoring, learning and governance committee structures with clinical and consumer participation.

A public Top End Health Service governance source documents clinical governance arrangements and review against national safety and quality expectations, but it cannot be treated as a whole-of-NT framework.

The 2026 national model defines six foundations: leading systems and organisational culture; partnering with patients, carers and consumers; building a healthy workforce culture; enabling high-quality and integrated clinical practice; managing and reducing risk; and using data for better care.
